scope: F-05 generic HTTP acceptance for ContractBOQ, QuantityMeasurement and PaymentClaim, including owner decision/payment record lifecycle

findings.endpoints: The three machines already use generic create/detail/command HTTP routes. No route or DTO generator change was needed.
findings.fixedGap: Payment record commands without externalSystemRef inherited the previous record's projected externalSystemRef before uniqueness validation. Engine.execute now clears that command-scoped input from the proposal when omitted; append-only paymentRecords remain unchanged.
findings.dto: Create wrapper is {roleAssignmentId, clientObjectId, payload}. ContractBOQ data is under record.boq. QuantityMeasurement and PaymentClaim fields are under record.data. Command wrapper is {roleAssignmentId, expectedVersion, payload, evidenceIds}; paths use kebab-case command names.
findings.fixtureLimits: The HTTP acceptance seeds the payment calculation Requirement/rule, accepted-and-released Inspection, and exact-target Decision fixtures directly inside committed store transactions. Evidence and Drawing refs are existing demo fixtures. ContractBOQ creation/approval/activation, quantity submission and verification, PaymentClaim submission/review/recommendation/owner adjustment/payment/correction/cancellation/close all use HTTP. These tests do not claim that the auxiliary Requirement, Inspection or Decision workflows were exercised through HTTP, nor do they claim pilot verification.

followup_AC_HO_01.scope: Separate CommissioningPackage, HandoverPackage and WarrantyClaim WorkItem machines with typed scoped Requirement applicability profiles, contract guards, immutable server snapshots, generated API/TypeScript schemas, real HTTP acceptance, and PostgreSQL inheritance.

endpoints.dto: All workflow records are WorkItems with fields under record.data. Create uses {roleAssignmentId, clientObjectId, payload}; command uses {roleAssignmentId, expectedVersion, payload, evidenceIds}.
endpoints.engine_hook: This branch relies on root-owned Engine/validator hook wiring from 9848203: initialize_create(engine,machine,record), check_guard(self,name,proposed,payload,party_id,role,command), and apply_effect(self,machine,command,proposed,payload,evidence_ids,party_id,role). Root must integrate those files before the branch runs without a hook overlay.

profile_configuration.commissioningProfile: Exact active scoped Requirement applicability must define requiredPrecommissioningItemIds, requiredTestProcedureRefs, requiredIntegratedTestRefs, and every requires* boolean. Test procedures must be current approved MethodStatement InformationItems.
profile_configuration.handoverProfile: Exact active scoped Requirement applicability must define a non-empty requiredDocumentSets list and both warrantyTriggerOnPartialHandover and warrantyTriggerOnFinalHandover. When a trigger is true, warrantyPeriodStartAt must be explicit; no date is inferred from effectiveAt.
profile_configuration.warrantyPeriod: Exact active scoped Requirement applicability must define startsAt, endsAt, responseDueHours and closeAuthorityActorGroup SUP or OWN. WarrantyClaim period start must equal the start recorded by its exact accepted Handover.
profile_configuration.configuration_boundary: Product Contract 34 leaves contract document sets, warranty trigger dates/period, response SLA and close authority contract-specific. The backend requires these explicit Requirement values and has no default that could infer a legal trigger. The acceptance fixtures seed trusted Requirements directly; production profiles must be provisioned through the project configuration path before a user can create these objects.

followup_AC_HO_01.acceptance_scope: Every F-07 WorkItem create/transition is exercised over HTTP. Trusted config and upstream accepted Inspection, Asset, InformationItem, Issue and Action fixtures are seeded directly. Retest evidence is uploaded through the HTTP evidence endpoint. No pilot/site verification is claimed.
